title: A hatch marker of a registry kind the shape does not declare is forbidden even inside a boundary (Undeclared clause), while a declared kind the boundary allows raises nothing

assert.why: A.4.2.4 [D1]: only the Undeclared clause covers the boundary's code for this kind

A.3.4.5: a registry hatch kind the shape does not declare lifts to Undeclared<Trust>; A.4.2.4: forbid hatch * adds effect.forbid(Undeclared<Trust>, [*], []), excepting no boundary, so the marker inside Trusted is a sound (manifest) contradiction; new because shim is a finest change (A.7.3.1)
A.7.4.3: shim is hatchComplete, which meets every hatch(ts) pair; the Undeclared clause has no hatch channel (A.4.5.2)
A.4.2.4 [D1]: the ts_ignore clause excepts Trusted, which allows ts_ignore, and no Hatch clause exists; coverage is met by hatchComplete
